channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Em debate de 'nerd', Tarcísio e Haddad cansam indecisos, mas cantam vitória
item.description: In a technically focused debate nicknamed the 'nerd debate', Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad failed to win over undecided voters, whose reactions were monitored in real time by their campaigns. Despite not swaying undecideds, both candidates declared victory afterward, each emphasizing their own performance.

item.title: Lula fez questao de slogan 'pronto pra mais', que fala de legado
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva directly influenced the choice of the re-election campaign slogan for 2026, 'Brazil ready for more', which aims to highlight his legacy and continuity project. The slogan was approved after several meetings with the campaign leadership, in which Lula emphasized the importance of conveying confidence in the country's future based on the advances of his administration.

item.title: Lula planeja ir à ONU durante a campanha, mas deve faltar ao Brics
item.description: President Lula plans to make only one international trip during the 2026 election campaign: a visit to the UN in New York to speak at the opening of the General Assembly in September, where he may meet with Donald Trump. He will skip the BRICS summit in India on September 12–13 due to campaign commitments, to be represented by Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira and possibly Finance Minister Dario Durigan.

item.title: Afinal, os debates mudam o resultado das urnas?
item.description: Presidential debates typically have a marginal impact on election results, except when a frontrunner makes a significant mistake. Historical examples show that strategic decisions to attend or avoid debates — such as Collor benefiting from a controversial debate in 1989, FHC skipping debates in 1994 and 1998 to avoid attacks, and Lula initially avoiding debates in 2006 due to the Mensalão scandal before participating in the runoff — can shape perceptions but rarely overturn established polling trends.

item.title: Com pauta amena, Congresso faz 1º esforço concentrado antes da eleição
item.description: The National Congress resumes deliberative sessions with a mild agenda, prioritizing consensus-driven projects and avoiding high-impact political votes ahead of the 2026 elections. Key government proposals — including the Public Security PEC, the 6×1 workweek repeal PEC, and the rare earths bill — remain stalled in the Senate due to lack of party leader agreement. The administration seeks to avoid legislative confrontations that could jeopardize Lula’s reelection, focusing instead on less controversial measures such as the Misogyny Bill, the Fuel PLP, and the MEI revenue cap expansion.

item.title: O assessor do Planalto que abriu o Ministério da Saúde para Luchsinger
item.description: In March 2025, Swedenberger Barbosa, former executive secretary of the Ministry of Health and presidential advisor, claimed he secured the release of R$ 40 million for Maranhão’s State Health Fund through coordination with lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, a friend of President Lula’s son. The funds, withheld due to a missing CIB resolution, were paid in August 2025. Governor Carlos Brandão stated he had no knowledge of Barbosa’s role in the release.

item.title: Cinco momentos em que Tarcísio e Haddad trocaram farpas no debate em SP
item.description: In the first debate between Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad for the São Paulo gubernatorial race, the candidates exchanged sharp remarks on public security, ties to Bolsonaro and Lula, and the U.S. tariff increase. Key moments included Tarcísio’s statement 'I have gratitude' toward Bolsonaro, Haddad’s mockery of Tarcísio as a 'concurseiro' and 'decoreba', and the metaphor of putting on the 'right hat' to defend national sovereignty. The debate grew heated, with direct attacks and efforts to frame each candidate as aligned with ideological extremes.

item.title: Após veto, Lula age para transformar o Cefet-MG em universidade
item.description: President Lula has submitted a revised bill to Congress to transform the Federal Center for Technological Education of Minas Gerais (Cefet-MG) into the Federal Technological University of Minas Gerais (UTFMG), following the veto of the original version due to unconstitutional legislative initiative. The new proposal, drafted by the Executive Branch, aims to comply with constitutional requirements and grant the institution administrative, financial, patrimonial, didactic, and disciplinary autonomy, expanding its role in teaching, research, extension, and technological innovation. While Cefet-MG leadership hopes for approval after over two decades of waiting, some members of the academic community oppose the transformation.

item.title: Sem Bolsonaro, sem furar bolha: como a campanha de Haddad avaliou 1º debate
item.description: Haddad's campaign assessed that Tarcísio de Freitas avoided mentioning Jair Bolsonaro during the first debate for the São Paulo gubernatorial race, interpreting it as an attempt to break out of the Bolsonaro-aligned bubble without directly associating with him. The debate focused on public security, education, and the economy, with Haddad attacking Tarcísio's record and the governor defending his administration while trying to nationalize the race by linking Haddad to Lula's federal government. Haddad's team said the debate had limited success in reaching beyond existing ideological bubbles.

item.title: Câmara envia ao STF relato de suposta "armação" contra vice de Flávio
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies sent to the Supreme Federal Court (STF) the testimony of a Rio de Janeiro merchant who claims the rape accusation against deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL), Flávio Bolsonaro’s vice-presidential running mate, was a fabricated scheme orchestrated by allies of Deputy Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ). The witness alleges a young woman was recruited to pose as the victim under a false name, 'Jailma'. The case was referred to the STF due to Farias’ privileged jurisdiction.

item.title: Vieira: Argentina precisa 'parar imediatamente' ataques ao governo Lula
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira stated that Argentina must 'immediately cease' its aggressions against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's government to restore normalcy in bilateral relations between Brazil and Argentina.

item.title: Faltas, críticas sobre segurança e Flávio ignorado marcam debates estaduais
item.description: The first round of state debates promoted by Band was marked by candidate absences, personal attacks, and criticism of public security. While PT supporters defended President Lula, PL allies barely mentioned Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL's presidential candidate, indicating a nationalization of issues and opposing strategies regarding political godfathers.

item.title: Redução na fila do INSS é bem-vinda, mas método usado desperta ceticismo
item.description: The INSS backlog dropped from 3.1 million to 1.6 million between February and July 2024, attributed to a government initiative with electoral motivation under President Lula. A sharp rise in benefit denials — from 395,000 to 669,000 per month between January and May — suggests the reduction was achieved through mass rejections, raising skepticism about the quality of service. The government aims to reduce the backlog to 1.3 million by September, ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Nunes irritado, risadas e 'cadeira de técnico': os bastidores do debate entre Haddad e Tarcísio na Band
item.description: The debate between Fernando Haddad (PT) and Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) on Band ended with backstage tension when São Paulo Mayor Ricardo Nunes (MDB) interrupted the broadcast to confront Haddad over claims that Wi-Fi contract funds were being diverted to the PCC and to finance a Bolsonaro biopic. Nunes accused Haddad of irresponsibility and even touched his arm, while allies tried to calm the situation. Despite the conflict, the candidates exchanged friendly greetings before and after the debate, and the audience responded with laughter and applause to controversial statements.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Até quando é possível se candidatar?
item.description: Parties, federations, and coalitions must register candidates by 7 p.m. on August 15, 2026, via the TSE system. If a party fails to register a chosen candidate, the candidate may file individually within 48 hours after the official list is published. Registration does not guarantee candidacy, as the Electoral Justice must still verify constitutional and legal eligibility requirements.

item.title: Desenrola Adimplentes começa hoje após ajustes para atrair os bancos
item.description: The Desenrola Adimplentes program, targeting informal workers with current or slightly overdue debts (under 90 days), begins implementation this Monday after rule adjustments to attract public and private bank participation. The government has made up to R$ 3 billion in federal funding available, allowing financial institutions to combine their own capital with the fund to renegotiate debts of up to R$ 15,000 at interest rates of up to 1.99% per month. Initially rejected by private banks, the initiative aims to address indebtedness among a previously underserved group, amid a record 82% of Brazilians in debt as of July.

item.title: Tarcísio defende vacina contra sarampo após fala de Eduardo Bolsonaro
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas defended measles vaccination in response to statements by Eduardo Bolsonaro, emphasizing the importance of immunization amid rising cases in São Paulo. He urged residents aged six months to 59 years to visit health posts, even if previously vaccinated, and noted the campaign runs until September 1. The remarks came ahead of his debate with Fernando Haddad, as the state reported 23 confirmed measles cases in 2026.

item.title: Nunes cobra Haddad em debate após fala sobre contrato investigado
item.description: After the electoral debate between Fernando Haddad and Tarcísio de Freitas, São Paulo Mayor Ricardo Nunes confronted Haddad for criticizing his administration and linking him to the investigated R$108 million contract with Instituto Conhecer Brasil (ICB) for Wi-Fi installation. Haddad had claimed Nunes, despite having R$80 billion in reserves, was indebting the city and implied the contract was being used to divert funds to the PCC and finance a Bolsonaro film. Nunes denied any involvement and asked Haddad not to associate him with the alleged misappropriation.

item.title: "Muleta" de Lula e "amigos do PL": Ciro e Elmano exploram apoios em debate
item.description: In the first debate for the Ceará gubernatorial race, Elmano Freitas (PT) accused Ciro Gomes (PSDB) of aligning with the PL and Bolsonaro’s political bloc, while Ciro countered that Elmano relies on Lula’s support as a political crutch. The exchange covered alliances, infrastructure, public security, and health, and included a notable slip when Elmano mistakenly cited Ciro instead of his brother Cid Gomes while listing allies.

item.title: Debate no PI: candidato do PP é cobrado por relação com Ciro Nogueira e Caso Master
item.description: In the first electoral debate in Piauí, promoted by Band, PP gubernatorial candidate Joel Rodrigues was challenged by Gustavo Henrique (Avante) over his professional and political ties to Senator Ciro Nogueira, who is under Federal Police investigation in the Banco Master case. Joel, who served as Ciro’s parliamentary aide in 2024, dodged the ethical questions, accusing Gustavo of acting on behalf of another candidate and emphasizing his own life story. The debate underscored ethical concerns and political alliances tied to federal figures and ongoing investigations.

item.title: Democracias sob ataque com ingerência eleitoral
item.description: Brazil prepares for the October 2026 elections amid growing concerns about potential foreign electoral interference, particularly from the United States. This threat is not isolated, as Europe similarly debates risks of interference in democratic processes. Experts warn that the vulnerability of democracies to external interventions is real and requires institutional vigilance.

item.title: Debate Band: Tarcísio e Haddad nacionalizam discussão e divergem sobre privatizações e economia
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad debated on Band regarding security, economy, and the nationalization of the state race, exchanging accusations about legacy, math skills, and ties to drug trafficking. The governor highlighted reduced homicide rates and the end of Cracólandia, while Haddad criticized the lack of federal recognition and linked Tarcísio to Bolsonarism and misinformation.

item.title: Congresso se apressa para destravar pautas; Lula negocia com Alcolumbre
item.description: Congress is accelerating the voting of stalled bills before the parliamentary recess, while President Lula seeks dialogue with Senator Davi Alcolumbre to unblock key government priorities in the Senate. The negotiations take place in the week leading up to the official start of the 2026 electoral race, with a focus on securing legislative progress before the campaign begins.

item.title: Debate virou programa para jornalista, torcida e campanha fazer cortes
item.description: The debate between Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad on Band featured few substantive exchanges and was primarily used to produce video clips for campaign purposes, emphasizing viral content over voter persuasion. Other debates held across the country that same Sunday followed the same pattern, prioritizing social media material over meaningful ideological discussion.

item.title: Garotinho critica Ruas por não defender Flávio Bolsonaro e diz que ‘não tem compromisso’ com Witzel
item.description: Anthony Garotinho criticized state deputy Douglas Ruas for failing to defend Senator Flávio Bolsonaro during the Band debate, calling his stance 'cowardly'. He also stated he has no commitment to former governor Wilson Witzel, despite Witzel's public support, and said he does not dictate his son Wladimir Garotinho's political choices, who is a pre-candidate for federal deputy under the PL party.

item.title: Tarcísio defende privatizar escolas: "Única preocupação será ensinar"
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas defended the privatization of public schools through Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs), stating that school staff would have only one concern: teaching. He justified privatizations as necessary, citing improvements in Sabesp after its privatization and criticizing Haddad for questioning concession contracts. Haddad responded that he would review contracts line by line and accused the government of lacking transparency in fiscal benefits granted to private companies.

item.title: Em São Paulo, governador Tarcísio e ex-ministro Haddad travam embate estadual com cara de presidencial
item.description: The Band debate for the São Paulo gubernatorial race featured only Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) and Fernando Haddad (PT), creating a direct confrontation with the tone and dynamics of a presidential runoff. The debate followed unique rules compared to other states, allowing candidates to manage their time via a time bank to present their arguments.

item.title: “Baixa essa bola”, diz Haddad após fala de Tarcísio sobre tráfico
item.description: During the São Paulo gubernatorial debate, Fernando Haddad (PT) told Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) to 'lower the ball' after the governor accused him of sharing a stage with a drug trafficker from the Favela do Moinho. Haddad countered by questioning why Tarcísio hadn't arrested the woman if he knew her involvement, stating he had no knowledge of her ties to drug trafficking. The debate also covered U.S. tariffs on Brazil, with Haddad framing the issue nationally and criticizing political support for the aggressor, while Tarcísio argued the tariffs harm São Paulo’s industry and proposed advancing ICMS credits to reduce the impact.

item.title: Quem é Igor Carvalho, repórter agredido durante debate da Band em SP
item.description: During the Band debate between Fernando Haddad and Tarcísio de Freitas, Igor Carvalho, a reporter for Brasil de Fato, was assaulted by a GloboNews cameraman in a dispute over recording space. The cameraman was removed from the Bandeirantes Group premises, and Carvalho received medical attention on-site, reportedly in good condition. Brasil de Fato condemned the incident as an attack on press freedom and the public's right to information.

item.title: Tarcísio e Haddad fazem debate duro e leal, com duelo sobre papel federal em resultados de São Paulo
item.description: In the first debate between Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad for the 2026 São Paulo gubernatorial race, the candidates clashed over the federal government's role in the state's performance, with Haddad crediting Lula's administration for infrastructure works and Tarcísio blaming Petista fiscal policy for hindering growth. The debate covered local issues such as Cracolândia, health, education, and security, while revisiting national topics like the pandemic, Operation Lava Jato, and the Dilma Rousseff administration, with both avoiding below-the-belt attacks despite data disputes and occasional provocations.

item.title: Haddad ressuscita ‘a culpa é de Campos Neto’ em debate com Tarcísio
item.description: In the first debate between São Paulo gubernatorial candidates, Fernando Haddad (PT) revived the accusation that 'the fault is Campos Neto's' while criticizing federal economic management, whereas Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) defended his record as former Infrastructure Minister and attacked the PT's alleged managerial incapacity. The Band-televised debate featured mutual accusations on inflation, public debt, and state governance.

item.title: Michelle Bolsonaro assiste debate de Celina ao lado de Damares e Bia Kicis
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro watched the Distrito Federal gubernatorial debate alongside Damares Alves and Bia Kicis, with the event shared by the senator on social media. Her appearance comes amid discussions about her potential Senate run, despite missing a PL event due to migraine. Allies suggest her campaign could center on 'staying home to care for her husband,' as Jair Bolsonaro continues to suffer from hiccups and remains under house arrest.

item.title: Debate no Ceará: Elmano de Freitas comete ato falho, diz que anda com Ciro Gomes e candidato reage; assista
item.description: During the first debate among candidates for governor of Ceará, Elmano de Freitas made a Freudian slip by stating he 'walks with Ciro Gomes', his political opponent, while listing allies such as Luizianne Lins and Lula. Ciro Gomes immediately retorted: 'Not with me', sparking reactions on social media. The debate also covered security, health, and education, featuring mutual accusations and tense exchanges between the candidates.

item.title: Tarcísio e Haddad fazem 1º debate nacionalizado, com dados e embates sobre PCC, tarifaço de Trump e privatizações
item.description: The debate between Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) and Fernando Haddad (PT) on Band focused on Trump's tariffs, the PCC, privatizations, and the nationalization of the race, with Haddad emphasizing federal government actions in São Paulo and Tarcísio initially rejecting, then adopting the strategy of linking the federal government to Lula. The exchange was data-driven, devoid of personal attacks, and followed a structured format with mediator and journalist questions, plus direct rebuttals.

item.title: Tarcísio e Haddad trocam farpas sobre educação, segurança e Bolsonaro
item.description: In the first electoral debate for governor of São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) and Fernando Haddad (PT) exchanged barbs on education, security, and Bolsonaro. Haddad criticized the decline in IDEB and alleged rise of organized crime, while Tarcísio highlighted the clearing of Cracolândia and actions against money laundering. Derrite, former security secretary and Senate candidate, reacted with laughter to the accusations.

item.title: Celina é alvo de adversários por crise do BRB no caso Master e tenta se descolar de Ibaneis em debate no DF
item.description: In the first debate for the Distrito Federal governor's race, Celina Leão faced criticism from opponents over the BRB bank scandal tied to the Master Bank fraud scheme, involving alleged theft of billions. She sought to distance herself politically from former governor Ibaneis Rocha, her former running mate, stating the DF would never again elect an ex-OAB president as governor. Candidates like Leandro Grass (PT) and José Roberto Arruda (PSD) condemned the BRB management, citing a projected deficit of R$8–13 billion and pledging investigations if elected.

item.title: Debate ao governo do RJ é marcado por ataques a Paes e associação do candidato de Flávio a Bacellar
item.description: The first debate for the Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial race featured intense attacks on absent frontrunner Eduardo Paes (PSD), who was labeled 'jelly man' by André Marinho (Novo), 'woman abuser' by Douglas Ruas (PL), and 'militia ally' by Anthony Garotinho (Republicanos). Ruas, backed by Flávio Bolsonaro and linked to Cláudio Castro and Rodrigo Bacellar, emphasized allegations of gender-based violence against Paes.

item.title: Mauro Vieira pede que Argentina pare agressões contra Brasil para normalizar relações
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira urged Argentina to halt its aggressions against Brazil to normalize bilateral relations, describing President Javier Milei's repeated offensive remarks as serious and damaging. He emphasized that the Brazil-Argentina relationship is fundamental and must be preserved regardless of political leadership, calling for mutual respect and immediate de-escalation. Vieira also dismissed Milei's accusations as false and stressed the importance of restoring diplomatic normalcy.

item.title: PCC e CV viram foco de discussão em debate entre Tarcísio e Haddad
item.description: In the debate between Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad for governor of São Paulo, the candidates discussed the advancement of organized crime, with Haddad accusing the PCC of having links with the Military Police and Tarcísio defending his government’s security record while citing operations against the PCC in the fuel and transport sectors, including the arrest of a PT councilman.

item.title: Cinegrafista da GloboNews é retirado da cobertura do debate após dar cabeçada em repórter
item.description: A GloboNews cameraman was removed from coverage of the Band debate between Fernando Haddad and Tarcísio de Freitas after headbutting a reporter during a scramble for camera space in the event's backstage area. The assaulted reporter received medical attention at the network, remained on assignment, and intends to file a police report.

item.title: Marina Silva critica Tarcísio sobre tarifaço e diz que governador colocou boné de Trump
item.description: Marina Silva, Senate candidate for São Paulo from the Rede party, criticized Governor Tarcísio de Freitas for his stance on the U.S. tariff increases, saying he 'put on a Trump hat' by supporting protectionist measures. She argued that Brazil must maintain its commercial sovereignty and not submit to external impositions that harm national industry and workers.

item.title: Ao chegarem a debate, Haddad foca em 4 anos de governo de concorrente e Tarcísio fala de futuro
item.description: In the electoral debate, Fernando Haddad, the PT candidate, focused on criticizing his opponent's four years in office, highlighting alleged failures in the current administration. Meanwhile, Tarcísio de Freitas, the incumbent governor and Republicanos reelection candidate, directed his speech toward the future, presenting proposals and a vision of continuity for São Paulo.

item.title: Cinegrafista da GloboNews é expulso de debate da Band após agredir repórter
item.description: A GloboNews cameraman was expelled from the Band debate in São Paulo after headbutting a Brasil de Fato reporter, who suffered a bleeding nose and was treated by firefighters. The incident took place in the station's parking lot shortly before the debate between Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad. Band security blamed the GloboNews employee and demanded his removal from the premises.

item.title: Coordenador da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro critica jantar de Lula com Moraes: ‘imparcialidade’
item.description: Senator Rogério Marinho, coordinator of Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign, criticized the dinner between President Lula and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre at the residence of Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, arguing it compromises impartiality and the separation of powers. Marinho stated that political agreements should not be negotiated in the homes of STF ministers, particularly when those judges are involved in high-impact electoral investigations. He emphasized that judges should not act as partisan intermediaries or guarantors of congressional successions.

item.title: Vacina de sarampo é ‘consagrada’ e ‘fundamental’, diz Tarcísio após Eduardo fazer campanha antivacina
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas urged residents to get measles vaccinations amid a state outbreak, calling the vaccine proven and essential. He addressed criticism of ally Eduardo Bolsonaro, who promotes anti-vaccine campaigns in the U.S., by affirming vaccine safety and encouraging public participation in immunization efforts.

item.title: 'Estamos enfrentando': Lula trata fila do INSS na base do gerúndio
item.description: The Lula government faces widespread criticism over the growing backlog at the INSS, leaving millions of Brazilians waiting for benefits and pensions. Although the issue began under Bolsonaro — with 2 million people in the queue at its peak — the current situation is seen as one of the main failures of the Lula administration, worsened by delays and inefficiency in social security processing.

item.title: Tarcísio e Haddad participam do primeiro debate das eleições para governador em SP
item.description: The current governor of São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), and former Finance Minister Fernando Haddad (PT) will participate in the first gubernatorial election debate, organized by Band, this Sunday at 8 p.m. The event marks the official start of the direct confrontation between the two leading candidates in the 2026 race.

item.title: Tarcísio e Haddad se enfrentam em primeiro debate pelo governo de SP
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) and former minister Fernando Haddad (PT) are facing off in the first debate for the São Paulo governorship in the 2026 elections, hosted by Band in partnership with TV Cultura, TV Gazeta, and Jovem Pan. The event takes place this Sunday, the 9th, marking the first direct confrontation between the two leading candidates for the state succession. Tarcísio arrived at the debate accompanied by the mayor of São Paulo.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Metrópoles repercute o 1º debate ao governo de SP. Siga
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) and Fernando Haddad (PT) face off in the first debate for the São Paulo gubernatorial race in the 2026 elections, held at Grupo Bandeirantes' studios. The event launches the open TV debate season across 12 states and the Federal District, featuring rules that grant candidates greater freedom to manage their time and move around the studio.

item.title: Quaest: Lula abre vantagem no Nordeste e Flávio lidera no Sul
item.description: Lula leads with 64% voting intention in the Northeast against 25% for Flávio Bolsonaro in a hypothetical runoff, according to Genial/Quaest poll. Another 9% of voters say they would not vote for either candidate. In the South, Flávio Bolsonaro leads, though specific margins for that region are not detailed in the excerpt.
